reviewerRole: Independent visual critic; no asset or scene authoring
scope: Blender full-source versus runtime still comparison only
verdict: Pass for native audition. No conspicuous reduction defect or recurrence of the rejected v1 punctures is visible in these two comparisons.
observations: The runtime retains continuous sack silhouettes and the dominant seam and fold structure. No new sharp black holes are visible on either sack.
The jug handle opening, neck and rounded moulded shell remain coherent. The cans retain readable openings, curved bodies and rolled rims.
The separate cardboard pieces preserve corrugation and torn outlines; the draped cloth retains its irregular edge and folds. Small stones still read as volumes rather than flat polygons.

The broad shape and object separation remain comparable to the detailed source at this image coverage. There is no visually justified reason in these images to restore the full source count wholesale.
remainingConcerns: The two objects occupy different positions in the render and are viewed under a slightly different perspective. This is a useful visual comparison, not a pixel-exact test of geometric equivalence.
Tiny can-wall, cardboard-edge and stone differences cannot be judged conclusively at this coverage. Inspect actual closest intended native views and an oblique moving pass before shipping.
The source concerns about subdued material separation, broad soft sack regions, ambiguous local joins and the thin surrounding base remain. Reduction preserving them does not resolve them.
Confirm that the native normal and roughness interpretation preserves this source appearance and that the base is naturally embedded into the paving or soil.
acceptance: The runtime candidate is suitable to install for controlled native audition. This does not accept final ground placement, motion stability, performance or AAA street quality.
